text: In 1946, the safety system for a plutonium core was a screwdriver. Held by hand. The core sat inside a shell that reflects neutrons back into it. Close the shell and the chain reaction runs away. Physicist Louis Slotin kept the halves apart with the tip of a screwdriver. Colleagues called it "tickling the dragon's tail". The screwdriver slipped. A flash of blue light. He knocked the shell apart and saved the others in the room, but he died nine days later. Some safety equipment is just optimism.
